mainTopic: שהיה and חזרה on a כירה, and whether food that is מצטמק ויפה לו may be left on the stove before שבת
overview: This amud asks when food may be left on a stove (כירה) from before שבת. First the גמרא tries to prove from two teachings that food which is מצטמק ויפה לו (gets better as it keeps cooking) may be left on the stove. Each time it pushes the proof off, because the coals there were covered (קטומה). It then finds the new points in those teachings: covered coals that flared up again still count as covered, and this holds even for very hot רותם coals. Next, רב ששת in the name of רבי יוחנן separates leaving food (שהיה) from returning it (חזרה). Leaving is allowed even on an uncovered stove, while returning needs a swept or covered stove. רבא shows that both halves are already implied by משניות. Then רבי יוחנן's view that even מצטמק ויפה לו may be left is set against רב and שמואל, who forbid it, and each community follows its own teachers. After stories about what great scholars did, רב נחמן rules that food that improves is forbidden and food that gets worse is permitted. He then lists which foods fall into each group. The amud ends as a new question is brought to רבי חייא בר אבא.

steps.title: Inference that shrinking-and-improving food is permitted
steps.stepSummary: From the previous teaching, the גמרא tries to prove that food which is מצטמק ויפה לו may be left on the stove.
steps.simpleTranslation: Learn from this: food that shrinks and gets better is permitted!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws a conclusion from the teaching of רבי אושעיא just quoted. It says that teaching proves you may leave food on the fire even if more cooking makes it better.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier teaching allowed leaving fully cooked food on the stove without separating between kinds of food. So the גמרא reasons that even food which improves with more shrinking is allowed. This matters because such food might tempt a person to stir the coals (חתייה).

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from this / conclude from it
Food that shrinks and improves by cooking more

phrases.english: Learn from this
phrases.notes: Introduces a proof drawn from the previous teaching

phrases.english: that food which shrinks and improves is permitted!

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁמַע מִינָּה מִצְטַמֵּק וְיָפֶה לוֹ מוּתָּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the discussion of רבי אושעיא's teaching earlier
steps.raayaObject: That מצטמק ויפה לו may be left on the stove
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי אושעיא's teaching, which permits leaving fully cooked food without separating between kinds of food

steps.title: Rejected: there the coals were covered
steps.stepSummary: The proof fails because in that case the coals were covered with ashes.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is different here, because he covered the coals with ashes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes off the proof. The teaching was about a stove whose coals were covered with ashes, so it proves nothing about an ordinary uncovered stove.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Covered coals (קטומה) remove the worry that a person will stir the fire. So the permission there comes from the covering, not from the type of food. This source cannot decide the question of מצטמק ויפה לו on an uncovered stove. רבי יוחנן's view comes in step 18, and רב נחמן's ruling in step 27.

keyTerms.meaning: He covered the coals with ashes

phrases.english: It is different here
because he covered it with ashes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of step 1
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof about מצטמק ויפה לו
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The case had covered coals, so the type of food played no role

steps.title: Then what is the point of the teaching?
steps.stepSummary: If the coals were covered, the permission is obvious, so why say it?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, what is it coming to tell us?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the rejection. If the stove was covered, everyone already knows you may leave food on it, so the teaching seems to add nothing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה already allows a covered stove. A teaching that only repeats this would be pointless. The גמרא now has to find something new in it.

keyTerms.meaning: What is there to say? (It is obvious)

phrases.english: If so
what is there to say?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the rejection in step 2
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that the teaching is about covered coals
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A covered stove is already permitted, so the teaching would teach nothing

steps.title: The new point: the fire flared up again
steps.stepSummary: The teaching was needed for the case where the covered coals reignited.
steps.simpleTranslation: The case where it flared up again was needed. You might have said that once it flared up, it goes back to its first status. So it teaches us that it does not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the new point is the case where the covered coals caught fire again. Even then, food may stay on the stove.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One could think that once the fire flares up, the covering no longer counts and the stove becomes forbidden like an uncovered one. The teaching says no: the covering done before שבת already showed that the person is not focused on the fire, so it still counts.

keyTerms.meaning: It was needed for him (to teach)

steps.whatToRemember: Covered coals (קטומה) that reignite still keep their permitted status.

phrases.english: The case of it flaring up was needed,
you might have said
that since it flared up
it goes back to its original status,
phrases.notes: Like an uncovered stove, which is forbidden

phrases.english: so it teaches us otherwise.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 3
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifies a new point (חידוש) in the teaching
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Once the fire flares up, the stove goes back to being forbidden
steps.terutzMaskana: Even after flaring up, the covered stove stays permitted

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: covered and reignited, even with broom-wood coals
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר בר חנה reports in the name of רבי יוחנן that on a covered stove that reignited, fully heated water and fully cooked food may be left, even over coals of רותם.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: If he covered the coals and they flared up again, one may leave on it water that is fully heated and food that is fully cooked, even if the coals are of broom wood.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new teaching from רבי יוחנן. It is very similar to the one just discussed but adds the case of רותם coals.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן permits leaving fully cooked food on covered coals that reignited. He adds that this holds even for רותם coals, which are very hot and burn a long time. This new statement will go through the same questions as the earlier teaching.

keyTerms.meaning: One may leave (food on the fire)
Coals of broom wood, which are very hot and long-lasting

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabba bar bar Ḥana said that Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
If he covered it with ashes and it flared up,
one may leave hot water on it
that was fully heated
and food that was fully cooked,
and even if they are coals of broom wood.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a parallel teaching to the one discussed in steps 1-4
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On covered coals that reignited, fully cooked food may be left, even over רותם coals

steps.title: Same inference from רבי יוחנן's teaching
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא again tries to prove that מצטמק ויפה לו is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: Learn from this: food that shrinks and gets better is permitted!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא repeats the same attempted proof, this time from רבי יוחנן's teaching. Because he did not separate between kinds of fully cooked food, the גמרא suggests that improving food is allowed too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words are the same as in step 1, but they are now aimed at a new source. The גמרא is checking whether this teaching settles the question.

phrases.english: Learn from this
that food which shrinks and improves is permitted!

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁמַע מִינָּה מִצְטַמֵּק וְיָפֶה לוֹ מוּתָּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws an inference from step 5
steps.raayaObject: That מצטמק ויפה לו is permitted

steps.title: Rejected again: the coals were covered
steps.stepSummary: The proof fails because רבי יוחנן was speaking about covered coals.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is different here, because he covered the coals with ashes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof the same way as before. The permission comes from the covering, not from the kind of food.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the stove was covered, there is no worry about stirring the coals. So the teaching tells us nothing about an uncovered stove.

phrases.english: It is different here
because he covered it with ashes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of step 6
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from רבי יוחנן's teaching

steps.title: Then why say it?
steps.stepSummary: If the coals were covered, the teaching seems obvious.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, what is it coming to tell us?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks again what new point the teaching has, if it is only about covered coals.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A covered stove is already permitted. The גמרא needs to find a חידוש in רבי יוחנן's words.

phrases.english: If so
what is there to say?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the rejection in step 7
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's teaching, read as being about covered coals

steps.title: The new point: it flared up again
steps.stepSummary: The teaching was needed for the case of reignited coals.
steps.simpleTranslation: The case where it flared up again was needed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the same answer as before. The new point is that the coals flared up again.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just as in step 4, the teaching tells us that a covered stove stays permitted even after the fire comes back to life. This answer will be challenged next.

phrases.english: The case of it flaring up was needed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 8
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A reignited stove might be forbidden

steps.title: That is the same as the earlier teaching
steps.stepSummary: The reignited case was already taught, so רבי יוחנן's teaching would be a repeat.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is the same as the other one!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא objects that the reignition point was already taught in the earlier teaching (steps 1-4). So רבי יוחנן's statement still seems to add nothing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two teachings should not say exactly the same thing. The גמרא needs to find something in רבי יוחנן's words that the earlier teaching lacked.

keyTerms.meaning: That is the same as that one

phrases.english: That is the same as that one!
phrases.notes: Points back to the earlier teaching

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 9
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that reignition is רבי יוחנן's new point
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The reignition case was already taught, so it would be a repeat

steps.title: The new point: broom-wood coals
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן's new point is that even very hot רותם coals are permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: The case of broom-wood coals was needed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי יוחנן's new point is the coals of רותם. Even with these, covering the coals is enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רותם coals stay very hot for a long time. So one might think covering them with ashes does not really cool them, and a person would still be focused on the fire. רבי יוחנן teaches that covering works even for these. This teaching still does not decide מצטמק ויפה לו. The גמרא takes up that question directly in steps 18-30.
steps.whatToRemember: Two teachings: covered coals that reignited stay permitted, and this holds even for very hot רותם coals. Neither one settles whether מצטמק ויפה לו is allowed on an uncovered stove.

phrases.english: The case of broom-wood coals
was needed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 10
steps.terutzResolutionType: Finds a different new point in the teaching
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Covering might not work for very hot רותם coals
steps.terutzMaskana: Covering works even for רותם coals

steps.title: רב ששת: leaving is allowed, returning is not
steps.stepSummary: On a stove heated with גפת or wood, food may be left even if not fully cooked, but once removed it may not be returned unless the coals are swept or covered.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said in the name of רבי יוחנן: On a stove that was heated with olive waste or wood, one may leave water that is not fully heated and food that is not fully cooked. If he took the food off, he may not put it back until he sweeps out the coals or covers them with ashes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ruling from רבי יוחנן through רב ששת. It separates two actions: leaving food on the stove (שהיה) and putting it back (חזרה).
steps.deeperAnalysis: Leaving food is allowed even on a hot, uncovered stove, and even when the food is not fully cooked. Returning food is stricter: it needs a swept or covered stove. This is a big step, because the משנה seemed to require sweeping or covering for any food on such a stove.

keyTerms.meaning: A stove (with spots for two pots)
Olive or sesame waste left after pressing; makes a hot fire
He may not put it back

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with the earlier cases. Here the food is NOT fully cooked, and the stove is NOT covered, yet leaving it is still allowed. Only putting it back requires a swept or covered stove.
steps.whyThisMatters: This ruling is the basis for the key split between שהיה and חזרה in the הלכות of food on the stove on שבת.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rav Sheshet said that Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
A stove that was heated with olive waste or with wood,
one may leave hot water on it
that has not been fully heated
and food that has not been fully cooked.
If he removed it, he may not return it
until he sweeps out the coals
or until he puts ashes on them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new teaching on whether the משנה is about שהיה or חזרה; step 13 spells out his answer
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Leaving is allowed even on an uncovered stove and with food not fully cooked; returning needs a swept or covered stove

steps.title: Why: the משנה is about returning
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that רב ששת reads the משנה as dealing only with returning food, so leaving food needs no sweeping or covering.
steps.simpleTranslation: He holds that our משנה taught about 'returning.' But as for leaving food, one may leave it even if the stove is not swept and not covered.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the reasoning behind רב ששת's ruling. He holds that when the משנה demands sweeping or covering, it is talking only about putting food back.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This answers the סוגיא's earlier question about what the משנה refers to. In רב ששת's view, the משנה's demand for גרוף or קטום applies only to חזרה. Leaving food (שהיה) has no such demand.

keyTerms.meaning: Swept out and covered with ashes

phrases.english: He holds:
phrases.notes: The גמרא explains רב ששת's view

phrases.english: our משנה taught about 'returning,'
but as for leaving, one may leave it
even though it is not swept
and not covered with ashes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning behind step 12
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה is about returning; leaving food needs no sweeping or covering

steps.title: רבא: both points are already in the משנה
steps.stepSummary: רבא objects that both halves of רב ששת's ruling are already taught.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: We already learned both of them.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא challenges רב ששת. He claims both parts of the ruling are already stated in משניות. This line sets up the two proofs that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An אמורא is not supposed to simply repeat a משנה. רבא is about to show where each half is already found.

phrases.english: Rava said:
We already learned both of them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב ששת's ruling as unneeded
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both halves are already in משניות, so the ruling adds nothing

steps.title: Leaving is taught: the bread with a crust
steps.stepSummary: The משנה about bread shows that partly baked food may be left in an unswept oven once a crust has formed.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned about leaving: One may not put bread into the oven at nightfall, nor a cake on coals, unless there is time for its surface to form a crust. This means that if its surface has formed a crust, it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא proves the first half from a משנה about bread. Once the bread has a crust, it may stay in the oven even though it is not fully baked and the oven is not swept.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Bread with a crust is still only partly baked, yet the משנה lets it stay in an ordinary oven. That is exactly רב ששת's point: food not fully cooked may be left without sweeping or covering.

keyTerms.meaning: A flat cake baked on coals
That its surface forms a crust

phrases.english: About leaving we learned:
One may not put bread
into the oven at nightfall
nor a cake on top of coals
unless there is time for its surface to form a crust.
This means that if its surface formed a crust, it is permitted.
phrases.notes: An inference: partly baked food may be left

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the first proof for רבא's claim in step 14
steps.raayaObject: That partly cooked food may be left on an unswept fire
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about bread and cakes (in the first פרק of שבת)

steps.title: Returning is taught: בית הלל's ruling
steps.stepSummary: בית הלל permit returning food only on a swept or covered stove, which is the second half of רב ששת's ruling.
steps.simpleTranslation: We also learned about returning: בית הלל say that one may even put it back. And בית הלל only went so far as to permit this on a stove that is swept or covered. But on one that is not swept or covered, they did not.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא proves the second half from our משנה. בית הלל allow returning food, but the משנה's context limits this to a swept or covered stove.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since בית הלל's permission to return food is said only about a גרופה and קטומה stove, it follows that returning onto an unswept stove is forbidden. That is רב ששת's second rule.

keyTerms.meaning: One may even put it back
They only went so far as (to permit)

phrases.english: About returning we also learned:
Beit Hillel say: one may even put it back.

phrases.aramaic: וְעַד כָּאן לָא קָשָׁרוּ בֵּית הִלֵּל
phrases.english: And Beit Hillel only went so far as to permit
on a stove that is swept or covered,
but on one that is not swept or covered,
they did not!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the second proof for רבא's claim in step 14
steps.raayaObject: That returning food needs a swept or covered stove
steps.raayaSupportSource: בית הלל's ruling in our משנה

steps.title: רב ששת was only spelling out the משנה's implication
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת's ruling is not a repeat; he teaches what can be inferred from the משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב ששת, too, came to teach us the inference from the משנה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers רבא's challenge. רב ששת did not mean to add a brand-new law; he was clarifying how to read the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both halves are found in משניות only through inference (דיוק), not in plain words. רב ששת's job was to state those inferences clearly, so that the משנה's sweeping requirement is read as being about returning.

keyTerms.meaning: An inference from the wording of the משנה

steps.whatToRemember: According to רב ששת in the name of רבי יוחנן: leaving food (שהיה) on an uncovered stove is allowed even if it is not fully cooked. Putting it back (חזרה) needs a swept or covered stove. He is spelling out the meaning of the משנה.

phrases.english: And Rav Sheshet, too,
teaches us the inference from the משנה.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַב שֵׁשֶׁת נָמֵי דִּיּוּקָא דְמַתְנִיתִין קָמַשְׁמַע לַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבא's challenge from steps 14-16
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines the purpose of the ruling as clarifying the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב ששת's ruling repeats what the משנה already says
steps.terutzMaskana: He states clearly what the משנה only implies

steps.title: רבי יוחנן permits leaving fully cooked food, even food that improves
steps.stepSummary: רב שמואל בר יהודה reports that רבי יוחנן allows leaving fully cooked food or fully heated water on a stove lit with גפת or wood, even if the food gets better as it cooks longer.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שמואל בר יהודה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: a stove that was heated with olive waste or with wood, one may leave on it a dish that is fully cooked and water that is fully heated, and even if the food shrivels and gets better.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ruling from רבי יוחנן about leaving food on an unswept stove before שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The fear in this סוגיא is that a person might stir the coals on שבת to help the food cook more. רבי יוחנן says that once food is fully cooked, we are not worried, even if longer cooking would make it tastier. This leniency about מצטמק ויפה לו is what the next steps challenge, because רב and שמואל forbid it.

keyTerms.meaning: A stove (a small stovetop with room for two pots)
Olive waste left after pressing, which burns very hot
We may leave (food on the fire from before שבת)
Shrivels and improves: food that gets better as it keeps cooking

phrases.english: Rav Shmuel bar Yehuda said
that Rabbi Yochanan said:
A stove that was lit with olive waste or with wood,
phrases.notes: The stove was not swept or covered.

phrases.aramaic: מְשַׁהִין עָלֶיהָ תַּבְשִׁיל שֶׁבִּישֵּׁל כׇּל צוֹרְכּוֹ
phrases.english: one may leave on it a dish that is fully cooked
and hot water that is fully heated,
and even if it shrivels and improves.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the discussion of רב ששת to a new ruling of רבי יוחנן about leaving food.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Fully cooked food may be left on an unswept stove, even if it shrivels and improves.

steps.title: A scholar objects: רב and שמואל forbid food that improves
steps.stepSummary: One of the רבנים challenges רב שמואל בר יהודה: both רב and שמואל say food that shrivels and improves is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: One of the רבנים said to רב שמואל בר יהודה: But רב and שמואל both say that food that shrivels and improves is forbidden!
steps.whatsHappening: A scholar challenges the ruling just quoted, because two great teachers said the opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge is aimed at the words 'even if it shrivels and improves.' רב and שמואל held that this kind of food is forbidden to leave, because the owner wants it to keep cooking and may stir the coals.

keyTerms.meaning: A certain one of the Rabbis (an unnamed scholar)

phrases.english: One of the Rabbis said
to Rav Shmuel bar Yehuda:
But Rav and Shmuel both say
that if it shrivels and improves, it is forbidden!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling of step 18.
steps.kashyaTarget: The leniency of 'even if it shrivels and improves'.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב and שמואל, two major authorities, forbid exactly this case.

steps.title: רב שמואל בר יהודה: I was only reporting רבי יוחנן's view
steps.stepSummary: רב שמואל בר יהודה answers that he knows שמואל forbids it; he was only telling what רבי יוחנן holds.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Do you think I do not know that רב יוסף said that רב יהודה said that שמואל said that food that shrivels and improves is forbidden? When I told you this, I was telling you רבי יוחנן's view.
steps.whatsHappening: רב שמואל בר יהודה answers the challenge by explaining that he was not ignoring רב and שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is no mistake here. There is simply a real disagreement: רבי יוחנן permits, while רב and שמואל forbid. He was only passing on רבי יוחנן's side of it.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that to say? Do you think?

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אַטּוּ לֵית אֲנָא יָדַע
phrases.english: He said to him: Do you think I do not know

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל
phrases.english: that Rav Yosef said that Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
If it shrivels and improves, it is forbidden?
When I told you,
I was saying it according to Rabbi Yochanan.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 19.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Recognizing a real disagreement between authorities
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The scholar thought רב שמואל בר יהודה had overlooked רב and שמואל.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is a real disagreement; the ruling was given only according to רבי יוחנן.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think רב שמואל בר יהודה took back his statement. He still reports רבי יוחנן's view; he just admits that רב and שמואל disagree.

steps.title: Each place follows its own teachers
steps.stepSummary: רב עוקבא from מישן tells רב אשי: you, who live near רב and שמואל, follow them; we will follow רבי יוחנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב עוקבא from מישן said to רב אשי: You, who are close to the place of רב and שמואל, act like רב and שמואל. We will act like רבי יוחנן.
steps.whatsHappening: A practical statement: different communities follow different sides of this disagreement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This shows that the question was not settled for everyone. Each place followed the authority of its own region. Those in רב and שמואל's area were strict, and others relied on רבי יוחנן's leniency.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב עוּקְבָא מִמֵּישָׁן לְרַב אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: Rav Ukva from Meishan said to Rav Ashi:
You, who are close to Rav and Shmuel,
act like Rav and Shmuel;
we will act like Rabbi Yochanan.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the disagreement in step 20 into practice for different communities.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Communities near רב and שמואל follow their strict view; others may follow רבי יוחנן.

steps.title: אביי asks: may one leave food on the stove?
steps.stepSummary: אביי asks רב יוסף what the law is about leaving food on the stove.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to רב יוסף: What is the law about leaving food on the stove?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי asks his teacher for the practical ruling. This sets up a back-and-forth of proofs from what people did.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After hearing the disagreement, אביי wants to know what to actually do. He is asking about food that shrivels and improves, the case under debate.

phrases.english: Abaye said to Rav Yosef:
What is the law about leaving food on the stove?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the practical law after the disagreement.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is it allowed in practice to leave food that shrivels and improves?

steps.title: רב יוסף: רב יהודה's food was left on the stove
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף answers that they used to leave food on the stove for רב יהודה, and he ate it.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: But they leave food on the stove for רב יהודה, and he eats it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף answers by pointing to what was done for his teacher, רב יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof is from practice: if a great scholar ate food that had been left on the stove, it must be allowed.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: הָא רַב יְהוּדָה מְשַׁהוּ לֵיהּ וְאָכֵיל.
phrases.english: He said to him: But they leave food for Rav Yehuda, and he eats it.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא רַב יְהוּדָה מְשַׁהוּ לֵיהּ וְאָכֵיל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It is allowed, as shown by רב יהודה's practice.

steps.title: אביי: רב יהודה was ill, so he is no proof
steps.stepSummary: אביי rejects the proof: רב יהודה was ill and in danger, so even on שבת itself food could be prepared for him. What about ordinary people?
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Leave aside רב יהודה. Since he is in danger, it is allowed to do things for him even on שבת itself. For me and you, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי pushes back: רב יהודה's case was special, so it proves nothing for regular people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A sick person in danger may have food heated even on שבת. So leaving food for him before שבת tells us nothing about a healthy person. אביי repeats his question for ordinary people.

keyTerms.meaning: Except for him, leave him aside
For me and you, what (is the law)?

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לֵיהּ: בַּר מִינֵּיהּ דְּרַב יְהוּדָה,
phrases.english: He said to him: Leave aside Rav Yehuda,
since he is in danger,

phrases.aramaic: אֲפִילּוּ בְּשַׁבָּת נָמֵי שְׁרֵי לְמֶעְבַּד לֵיהּ.
phrases.english: even on Shabbat itself it is permitted to do it for him.
For me and you, what is the law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof given in step 23.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from רב יהודה's practice.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רב יהודה was a sick person in danger, a special case that does not apply to healthy people.

steps.title: רב יוסף: In סורא they leave food, as רב נחמן בר יצחק did
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף answers that in סורא they leave food on the stove, since רב נחמן בר יצחק, a very careful person, had food left for him and ate it.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: In סורא they leave food on the stove, because רב נחמן בר יצחק was a man of careful deeds, and they would leave food for him and he would eat it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף gives a new answer based on a healthy and very careful person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This time the proof cannot be pushed away by saying the person was sick. רב נחמן בר יצחק was known for being exact in מצוות, so if he ate such food, it must be allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: Sura, a major Torah center in Babylonia
A master of deeds: a person very careful in מצוות

phrases.english: He said to him: In Sura they leave food on the stove,

phrases.aramaic: דְּהָא רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק מָרֵי דְעוֹבָדָא הֲוָה,
phrases.english: for Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak was a man of careful deeds,
and they would leave food for him and he would eat it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the renewed question of step 24.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It is allowed, as shown by the practice of the careful רב נחמן בר יצחק in סורא.

steps.title: רב אשי's unclear evidence from רב הונא's fried fish
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי saw that fried fish was left on the stove for רב הונא and he ate it, but he did not know why: did רב הונא permit improving food, or was the dish one that gets worse because it has flour?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: I stood before רב הונא, and they left for him a dish of fish fried in oil, and he ate it. I do not know if it was because he holds that food that shrivels and improves is allowed, or because the dish has flour in it, so it shrivels and gets worse.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי adds a story about what he saw, but admits it does not prove anything clearly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story could support the lenient view, but there is another way to explain it. If the fish dish has flour, it actually gets worse with long cooking, and that kind of food is allowed by everyone. So the proof stays uncertain.

keyTerms.meaning: A dish of fish fried in oil
Shrivels and gets worse: food that is ruined by more cooking

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: קָאֵימְנָא קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב הוּנָא
phrases.english: Rav Ashi said: I stood before Rav Huna,
and they left for him a dish of fish fried in oil, and he ate it,
and I do not know if it is because he holds
that food that shrivels and improves is permitted,

phrases.aramaic: אִי מִשּׁוּם דְּכֵיוָן דְּאִית בֵּיהּ מִיחָא —
phrases.english: or because, since it has flour in it,
it is food that shrivels and gets worse.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another practice story on the same question, but it cannot decide the question.
steps.raayaObject: Whether food that shrivels and improves may be left on the stove.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב הונא ate fried fish left on the stove, but the reason is unclear.
steps.confusionAlert: This is not a full proof. רב אשי himself says the story can be explained in two ways, so it proves nothing for sure.

steps.title: רב נחמן: improving food is forbidden, worsening food is permitted
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן rules that food that shrivels and improves may not be left, but food that shrivels and gets worse may be left.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: Food that shrivels and improves is forbidden. Food that shrivels and gets worse is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן gives a clear ruling that sides with the strict view of רב and שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If longer cooking helps the food, the owner wants it to keep cooking, so we fear he will stir the coals. If longer cooking ruins the food, he has no reason to stir, so it is allowed.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said:
Food that shrivels and improves is forbidden;
food that shrivels and gets worse is permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן מִצְטַמֵּק וְיָפֶה לוֹ אָסוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After unclear stories, gives a clear rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Food that shrivels and improves is forbidden to leave; food that shrivels and gets worse is permitted.
steps.whyThisMatters: This rule is the base for the guide that follows, which sorts foods into the two groups.

steps.title: General rule: dishes with flour get worse, except turnip
steps.stepSummary: The general rule is that any dish with flour gets worse with long cooking, except a turnip dish, which improves even with flour.
steps.simpleTranslation: The general rule: any dish that has flour in it shrivels and gets worse, except a turnip dish. Even though it has flour, it shrivels and improves.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now explains how to tell which group a food belongs to.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Flour normally makes a dish stick and burn with long cooking, so it gets worse and is allowed. A turnip dish is the exception: it gets better with long cooking, even with flour, so it is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: The general rule of the matter

phrases.english: The general rule of the matter:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל דְּאִית בֵּיהּ מֵיחָא — מִצְטַמֵּק וְרַע לוֹ,
phrases.english: any dish that has flour in it shrivels and gets worse,
except for a turnip dish,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאַף עַל גַּב דְּאִית בֵּיהּ מֵיחָא —
phrases.english: which, even though it has flour in it,
is a food that shrivels and improves.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how to apply רב נחמן's rule to real foods.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Dishes with flour count as getting worse, except a turnip dish, which counts as improving.

steps.title: The turnip exception only applies with meat and not for guests
steps.stepSummary: The turnip dish improves only when it has meat. And even with meat, that is only when it is not being prepared for guests; for guests it counts as getting worse.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is said only when it has meat in it. But if it has no meat, it shrivels and gets worse. And even when it has meat, we only said this when it is not needed for guests. But if it is needed for guests, it shrivels and gets worse.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא narrows the turnip exception with two conditions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A turnip dish improves with long cooking only if it has meat. Even then, if it is meant for guests, overcooked food looks bad to serve, so for that host it counts as getting worse. Whether food 'improves' depends on what the person wants from it.

phrases.english: And this applies only when it has meat in it,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל לֵית בֵּיהּ בִּשְׂרָא — מִצְטַמֵּק וְרַע לוֹ הוּא.
phrases.english: but if it has no meat in it, it shrivels and gets worse.
And even when it has meat in it,

phrases.aramaic: לָא אֲמַרַן אֶלָּא דְּלָא קָבָעֵי לֵהּ לְאוֹרְחִין,
phrases.english: we only said this when he does not need it for guests,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל קָבָעֵי לֵהּ לְאוֹרְחִין — מִצְטַמֵּק וְרַע לוֹ.
phrases.english: but if he needs it for guests, it shrivels and gets worse.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the turnip exception from step 28.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A turnip dish counts as improving only if it has meat and is not meant for guests.
steps.confusionAlert: The same dish can be 'improving' for one person and 'getting worse' for another. It depends on the purpose, such as serving guests.

steps.title: Figs, porridge, and dates get worse with long cooking
steps.stepSummary: Dishes of figs, porridge, and dates all shrivel and get worse, so they may be left on the stove.
steps.simpleTranslation: Figs, porridge, and dates shrivel and get worse.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the guide by listing more foods that get worse with long cooking.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These foods are spoiled by too much cooking, so the owner has no reason to stir the coals. According to רב נחמן's rule, they may be left on the stove.

phrases.english: Figs, porridge, and dates
shrivel and get worse.

steps.triggerLanguage: לַפְדָּא דַּיְיסָא וְתַמְרֵי מִצְטַמֵּק וְרַע לָהֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds more examples to the list of foods that get worse.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: According to רב נחמן, food that improves with cooking may not be left on an unswept stove, but food that gets worse may be. Examples of food that gets worse are dishes with flour (except a turnip dish with meat that is not for guests), figs, porridge, and dates.
steps.whatToRemember: The key question is whether more cooking helps the food or hurts it. If it helps, we fear stirring the coals, so it is forbidden. If it hurts, it is permitted.

steps.title: A question is brought to רבי חייא בר אבא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא introduces a question that the scholars asked רבי חייא בר אבא. The content of the question comes in the next line.
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked a question of רבי חייא בר אבא:
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא tells us that a question was put to רבי חייא בר אבא, and the actual question will come in the very next line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase בעו מיניה signals a real בעיא, meaning a genuine question that the scholars did not know how to answer, not an attack on someone's view. Naming the person being asked tells us whose tradition or ruling will settle the matter. Nothing has been asked or ruled yet, so hold on and read the next line.

keyTerms.meaning: They asked of him. This phrase opens a genuine question put to a scholar.
A genuine question that the scholars are unsure about, as opposed to a קשיא, which is a challenge.
An אמורא who is asked the question here and is expected to answer it.

steps.confusionAlert: Don't look for the question in this line, because it isn't here yet. בעו מיניה only announces that a question is coming. It is a real request for information, not an objection.

phrases.english: They asked of him
phrases.notes: This is the standard formula for raising a genuine question (בעיא).

phrases.english: of Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba:
phrases.notes: This names the scholar being asked. The question follows in the next line.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּעוֹ מִינֵּיהּ מֵרַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the conclusion about which foods may be left on the stove (step 30), the גמרא opens a new question on the topic of food on the stove for שבת.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A question put to רבי חייא בר אבא, likely on a related case of food on the stove. Its exact content is stated in the next line of the source.
